title: Zakariya Khan’s Proclamation Turns Persecution into Policy

blocks.text: This page shows repression taking formal legal shape. A written proclamation across Lahore orders that even Sikhs quietly farming or trading are not to be spared if they keep unshorn hair, turning visible Sikh identity into a mark for state violence.

Bounties and permissions follow from that decree. Informers are rewarded, looters are indulged, and people are encouraged to hand over Singhs for questioning, imprisonment, or death, which lets private greed work together with official persecution.

The poem then personalizes the suffering through stories of betrayal, family loss, and the seizure of elders linked with Bhai Taru Singh. By combining policy with memory, the page shows how anti-Sikh violence spread from courtly order into village society.
